title: Apply to restrict dealing on a vehicle
summary: You can place a dealing restriction on a vehicle at a Service NSW Centre if you need to stop it from being sold.
intro:
If you need to stop a vehicle being sold, you can place a dealing restriction on it at a Service NSW Centre.

A dealing restriction is placed on a vehicle when ownership is disputed. Registration can be renewed on the vehicle, but it can't be transferred or re-established.
what_you_need: A police report or COPS Event Number (if applicable)
A copy of the will/last testament if you are the executor of the estate (if applicable)
Authorisation from the company, if you are representing their directions (if applicable)
Evidence that you are a company director (if applicable)
The PDF form – 'Dealing Restriction Application' (with a daytime contact number included)
Documentary evidence that legal proceedings have commenced, or a letter from a legal representative that legal proceedings are about to commence
Written proof of the relationship between the parties (for example, a letter from a solicitor outlining the relationship)

how_to_steps.text: Make sure you've attached all the required documents.
Visit a service centre and submit your application.

faqs.a: A dealing restriction is placed on a vehicle when ownership is disputed. While registration can be renewed, the vehicle cannot be transferred or re-established.

faqs.q: Where can I place a dealing restriction?
faqs.a: You can place a dealing restriction on a vehicle at a Service NSW Centre.

faqs.q: What do I need to apply for a dealing restriction?
faqs.a: You need various documents, including proof of identity, the application form, and evidence related to the dispute.
